title: Document-native systems treat unstructured construction documents as first-class, queryable data
content:
"Document-native systems" (BIM Services LLC, Mar 2026): digital tools designed to work **directly with unstructured construction documents** — specifications, contracts, submittals, compliance files — rather than only with structured data.

In practice:
- Automatically extracting submittal requirements from specifications
- Generating structured outputs (Excel/Word today)
- Natural-language queries over project documents: *"List all submittals under Division 07"*
- Turning hours of manual document review into minutes

Framing on the human role: AI handles repetitive document review, information extraction, and data organization; engineers, BIM coordinators, and managers keep judgment, planning, and site execution — a productivity tool, not a replacement.

The concept is externally-validated demand for what Powerhouse document models already are, with one decisive difference: document-native *retrofits* (extract from static files, emit Excel) recover structure after the fact, while documents **born structured** as document models never lose it. The extraction approach is still relevant as the migration path — LLM-scanning legacy analog documents into structured models is exactly the on-ramp proposed in the DT BAU engagement (02:07:18).
description: Tools that read specs, contracts and submittals directly: extract requirements, emit structured output, answer queries like 'submittals under Division 07'. Retrofit structure vs. born-structured.
